name: Ron Tototz
summary: Larry's bunk mate and closest companion in the collection — "he's Polish," from Des Moines, Iowa. He appears with Larry from the first weeks at Nha Trang (VN-0025, with Parr) through the Cholon pool outings (VN-0004, VN-0005), the beach at Nha Trang (VN-0021, VN-0022), their quarters (VN-0001, VN-0002, VN-0003), and hooch T 123 with Sarge the monkey, which he hated (VN-0017). Ron was with Larry during the bathroom shooting incident. Identified in August 2026 as Ronald E. Totosz of Des Moines (October 10, 1941 – August 12, 2004): a Des Moines Register news item of November 2, 1962 records his Army enlistment at age 21 from 1211 Merle Hay Road, a three-year term that brackets Larry's Vietnam tour; he later worked twenty-five years as a bio tech at Iowa Methodist Hospital, and rests with his wife Okhe at the Merle Hay mausoleum in Des Moines.
researchNotes: Identified 2026-08-16 (issue #58) as Ronald E. Totosz — the only Ronald of this rare Polish surname found anywhere in the country, in exactly the city Larry named. Documented: born October 10, 1941 in Chicago (the family moved from the Calumet City area to Des Moines; his mother Irene Totosz died in Des Moines in 1983); U.S. Army enlistment reported in the Des Moines Register of November 2, 1962; died August 12, 2004 in Ankeny, obituary in the Register of August 18, 2004; Find a Grave memorial 190642286. His death was earlier than Larry's "about ten years ago" — a familiar compression of time in long recollection. Still open: a document placing him in Vietnam and in Larry's unit (morning reports via NPRC once the unit question settles), and contact with his family, who may hold his photographs and letters from 1964–65.
